title: Change a date string to a datetime object
description:
Today is 5 December, 2019. Change this time string to time.

Python-Gym adaptation: implement as parse_date_string(date_string), which takes a date string in the same "5 December, 2019" style (day, full month name, comma, 4-digit year) and returns the corresponding datetime.datetime object.
starter_code:
import datetime

def parse_date_string(date_string):
    # your code here
    pass
hints: The datetime module has a method that turns a string into a datetime object given a matching format, the mirror image of strftime.
The format codes you need are %d for the day, %B for the full month name, and %Y for a 4-digit year, separated the same way as in the string.
Use datetime.datetime.strptime(date_string, "%d %B, %Y") to parse the string into a datetime object.
expected_behavior: Given a date string like '5 December, 2019', returns the equivalent datetime.datetime object.
explanation: datetime.datetime.strptime(string, format) parses a string into a datetime object using the given format codes. "%d %B, %Y" matches a day number, a full month name, a comma, and a 4-digit year - exactly the shape of "5 December, 2019" - and produces a datetime.datetime with the time set to midnight since no time was given.
